plan.summary: BRO-5517 follow-up: ten show notes, which print on the /biz show card, still quoted tax credit guesses written before the state paid or allocated the award the recoupment model now counts (scripts/lib/ny-tax-credit.js). Glengarry Glen Ross said "Expected ~$1.9M" (paid $2.7M), An Enemy of the People "~$1.3M" (paid ~$2.3M), Othello "~$2M" and Romeo + Juliet "up to $1.75M" (each allocated $3M); Buena Vista Social Club’s "Eligible for $3M" is now a payment; Art has no award listed and its "Eligible for $3M" named the cap as if owed. Four more still said "Eligible for $3M" after the award: Water for Elephants and The Great Gatsby were paid $3M (Jan 2025), Death Becomes Her and Sunset Boulevard allocated $3M (Aug 2025). Only the tax credit sentence changes in each note. Found by the new taxCreditNoteConflicts check (validate-data.js warning; audit-commercial-data.js weekly sweep).
steps: Each action replaces one sentence of the notes; the rest of each note is unchanged.
After apply, taxCreditNoteConflicts returns no conflict for any record.

actions.oldValue: Kieran Culkin, Bob Odenkirk, Bill Burr revival (all Broadway debuts). $7.5M cap (SEC confirmed). Recouped in 9 weeks (May 12, 2025). Broke Palace Theatre box-office record ($2.4M gross). Weekly nut ~$925K — early weeks roughly broke even, then $1M+ weeks drove quick recoupment. Expected ~$1.9M NY state tax credit (25% of costs). Run extended twice. All-male cast throughout.

Paid a $2.7M NY tax credit by Jun 2026 (Bloomberg Tax). Run extended twice. All-male cast throughout.
actions.description: glengarry-glen-ross-2025: the note tax credit sentence matches the award the model counts: paid about $2.7M by Jun 2 2026 (Bloomberg Tax, from ESD records), not the ~$1.9M expected.

actions.oldValue: Jeremy Strong and Michael Imperioli in Amy Herzog's Ibsen adaptation. $5.5M cap recouped during run at Circle in the Square (840 seats). Broke CITS weekly gross record 16 times during run. Final week record: $1,266,338 (prev record $917K by Hugh Jackman in The River). Joined Broadway's $1M Club for weekly grosses — almost unheard of for a non-musical. Strong won Tony for Best Actor. Digital lottery + cancellation line ensured 100%+ capacity some weeks. Eligible for ~$1.3M tax credit.

actions.oldValue: Denzel Washington & Jake Gyllenhaal. $9M cap. Recouped in 9 weeks (May 1, 2025). Shattered weekly Broadway play record with $2.82M gross (topping Harry Potter). Tony snub but producers announced recoupment as rejoinder. Washington likely had gross percentage deal.

Recouped week ending Dec 14, 2025 (~13 weeks into 16-week run). Weekly nut ~$725-750K — surprisingly high for 3-actor play due to star salaries (~$350K/week combined) and premium Broadway Journal ad spend. Averaged $1.2-1.8M gross at ~99% capacity. Matthew Warchus directed (also directed original 1996 production). Eligible for $3M NY tax credit.

actions.oldValue: Jamie Lloyd-directed revival starring Nicole Scherzinger. $15M capitalization. Weekly nut ~$950K. Won Tony for Best Actress (Scherzinger). Producer J.J. Powell confirmed $6M loss (~40% of cap) despite selling out and grossing $60M+ total. Jamie Lloyd invested $4M personally (~27% of cap) — unusual director-as-investor arrangement. Lloyd likely recouped his loss via director royalties (~1-2% of gross over 10 months). ALW's Really Useful Group took substantial composer/rights royalties. Scherzinger had high salary + possible gross percentage. Highest gross $2.5M in final week. Eligible for $3M tax credit (would reduce net loss to ~$3M).
